sortableColumns — VERIFIED: value ['name','sku','price','stock_quantity','created_at','updated_at'] (page.tsx:175) is EXACTLY the intersection of the rendered column keys {name,sku,price,stock_quantity,created_at,updated_at,action} and the products allowlist {created_at,updated_at,name,sku,price,stock_quantity,id} (SORT_ALLOWLISTS.products, admin-table.ts). Reset rules — VERIFIED: sort header click → loadProducts(token,{resetCursor:true,sort:next}) (page.tsx:180); search 'Cari' → {resetCursor:true} (page.tsx:152); page change → {cursor:nextCursor} preserving sortRef.current + current filter state (page.tsx:191-193).
Null timestamps — VERIFIED: null created_at/updated_at render '—' via formatDateTime; page.test.tsx asserts cells[4]/cells[5] contain U+2014 and no 'Invalid Date' in the DOM.

Scope — VERIFIED: `git diff 532ab8e..15f2f18 --name-only` lists exactly the 5 in-scope files (ProductController.php, ProductTest.php, products/{page.tsx,api.ts,page.test.tsx}); no out-of-scope files touched across the 4 commits.

Independent verification — ProductTest 13 passed / 57 assertions; `npx jest src/app/admin/products` 15 passed; `npx jest src/app/admin/outlets` 18 passed (dummy-guard intact); full `npx jest` 237 passed / 33 suites; `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors.

strengths: Backend change is strictly additive and surgical (+8/-1, one block): meta.summary derived from the SAME filtered builder as meta.total, so the strip can never disagree with the total; out_of_stock reuses the identical eligibility filter (inactive-supplier exclusion covered by a dedicated test).

fetchProducts is left untouched and fetchAdminProducts is a clean parallel export, preserving the dummy-guard contract while letting the page consume meta.total/meta.summary with a tolerant fallback when total/summary are absent.

sortableColumns derives from the real allowlist∩rendered-keys contract (verified against SORT_ALLOWLISTS.products); default created_at header is wired end-to-end to aria-sort='descending' and non-sortable 'Aksi' is inert (tested).
sortRef/cursorRef keep sort/cursor out of loadProducts' dependency list, avoiding the mount-effect reset-on-every-change trap; reset rules are applied explicitly at each call site.

Dummy path achieves real parity through the shared compareRows/paginate helpers (no bespoke sort logic), covering created_at-DESC→id-DESC fallback, offset slice, total=filtered.length and summary, with zero network.

Tests assert rendered behavior (aria-sort, em-dash cells, summary text, fetch URLs, dummy ordering) rather than tautologies, and null-timestamp + paging edge cases are exercised through the real component.
Only in-scope files changed; must-not-have functions verified byte-identical to parent.

issues.description: page.test.tsx is 409 lines (four nested describe blocks). Test files are naturally long and this mirrors the already-approved outlets page.test.tsx (399 lines), so it is not treated as a blocking split; noted only as a maintainability observation.

Because loadProducts is a useCallback keyed on `search` and the mount effect depends on loadProducts, changing the search input triggers an immediate fetch (cursor=0) on each keystroke in addition to the explicit 'Cari' button, so there is no debounce and a request may fire per keystroke. This is the established pattern inherited from the outlets page (same shape) and does not violate the spec's reset rule, so it is non-blocking.
